PullRequest.Title: agentHost: support managed OpenTelemetry file export
PullRequest.Body:

Fixes microsoft/vscode#340964

## Summary

Wire the shared Copilot managed `telemetry.filePath` into Agent Host's existing file-export settings.
A managed file destination takes precedence over collector configuration and enables OTel unless
managed `enabled:false` is present. Use the existing generic managed-settings normalization and
native watcher contract rather than adding malformed-value metadata or synthetic empty markers.

- Expand managed home-relative paths on the exporting host; create missing parent directories and append.
- After file selection, log path-resolution/write errors without blocking chat or switching to a collector.
- Malformed values follow existing channel behavior. Generic omission can leave a collector effective;
  a directly projected empty string retains its existing file-selection behavior.
- Keep existing restart behavior and managed-endpoint SQLite parity: native Copilot traces export
  directly to the managed destination; separately enabled SQLite retains Agent Host-owned records.
  No new native-to-SQLite bridge or SDK trace-subscription API.
- Update the generated policy catalog, documentation, and focused policy/path/SQLite tests.

Extension OTel and Copilot App are not included.

## Validation

Checks executed locally on macOS; successful earlier results are reused where inputs are unchanged:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/otel/agentHostOTelService.integrationTest.ts --reporter dot` — 42 passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/policy/test/common/copilotManagedSettings.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/policy/test/node/nativeManagedSettingsService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/test/browser/managedSettings.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentHostOTelPolicy.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentService.test.ts --reporter dot` — 197 passed.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/policy/common/copilotManagedSettings.ts src/vs/platform/policy/node/nativeManagedSettingsService.ts src/vs/platform/policy/test/common/copilotManagedSettings.test.ts src/vs/platform/policy/test/node/nativeManagedSettingsService.test.ts src/vs/workbench/services/accounts/test/browser/managedSettings.test.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/agentHostOTelPolicy.test.ts` — passed.
- `npm run export-policy-data -- --skip-transpile` — passed; catalog unchanged by this simplification.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Four new expectations reproduced the old normalization/metadata behavior before the production
cleanup. Independent source review of the simplification passed with no findings. The client-only
policy exporter emitted missing-extension activation warnings; no extension E2E claim is made.

## Draft status / remaining work

This is source integration, not a ready-to-ship feature. Matching runtime/SDK packages have not
been consumed here, and server delivery must support the new field. No new policy-watcher package
or invalid-value metadata API is required.
Real managed-account/packaged-provider end-to-end and Windows/Linux validation remain outstanding.

Known review findings intentionally not addressed in this draft:

1. Agent Host and native path resolution can differ for symlink paths containing `..`.
2. Home expansion via `untildify` interprets replacement tokens in home names containing `$`.
3. Paired literal percent signs in filenames are rejected too broadly.

Inactive collector validation was addressed separately in the Settings Engine changes.
The branch retains its original development base; it has not been rebased during draft creation.

## Policy-watcher scope

The extra native metadata API proposed in microsoft/vscode-policy-watcher#82 is no longer needed.
This PR uses the existing watcher contract.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path is direct: each non-empty `forwardSpans` queues `_append`; `_append` unconditionally awaits `fs.mkdir` when the new managed option is true; the same class queue serializes that operation before `appendFile`. Tests explicitly send successive batches with the option enabled. Only exact event volume and filesystem latency vary.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem mkdir operations and queued telemetry buffers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Cost grows linearly with non-empty telemetry batches: after the first successful parent creation, each batch still adds one recursive mkdir call. The queue has effective concurrency 1, so each added call directly lengthens the serialized drain path.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: excessive filesystem I/O and lower telemetry-export throughput
Findings.PreviousBehavior: File forwarding previously issued only the append operation per batch; it did not perform parent-directory creation. The PR adds one mkdir boundary per managed-file batch rather than only for the cold first write.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Managed file forwarding now performs recursive parent-directory creation for every queued append, including warm writes after the directory was already created.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 233 adds `await fs.mkdir(dirname(this._options.filePath), { recursive: true })` inside `_append`, and AgentHostOTelService now sets `createParentDirectories: this._config.managedFilePath`; therefore every managed-file call to `forwardSpans` executes this new filesystem operation.
Findings.Title: Create managed export directories only once
Findings.Impact: Managed file export generates a redundant filesystem operation ahead of every telemetry write. On busy sessions or slower/network-backed managed destinations this lowers export throughput, extends flush/shutdown latency, and can let queued serialized batches retain their JSON strings longer.
Findings.Evidence: `FileForwarder.forwardSpans` queues one `_append` per non-empty decoded/synthetic batch. The changed `_append` calls `fs.mkdir(..., { recursive: true })` whenever `createParentDirectories` is true, without a success flag or promise cache, and only then calls `appendFile`. `AgentHostOTelService` enables the option for every managed path. Host session, turn-timing, first-response, user-interaction, and received OTLP batches all reach this forwarder, so a long session repeatedly traverses the same parent path.
Findings.Recommendation: Memoize successful parent setup in the forwarder (for example, a shared initialization promise or ready flag), and clear it only on failure so later batches can still retry after repair. Then each process lifetime pays mkdir once on success while preserving the documented recovery behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply managed telemetry.filePath and start or restart the local Agent Host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Managed settings are normalized/projected, configuration policy values are read, and `buildAgentHostOTelEnv` composes the child environment before the existing Agent Host spawn can complete. Managed-path validation is synchronous string/path work during AgentHostOTelService construction; it performs no filesystem access.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retrieve the managed-settings response that may now contain telemetry.filePath.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One field in the existing managed-settings response; no extra request per policy leaf.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same managed-settings response was fetched and normalized without consuming telemetry.filePath.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing response must arrive for managed policy to apply, but this diff only consumes another field and does not add a network round trip.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn or replace the local Agent Host with the composed OTel environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing host process per spawn/replacement event, not one process per setting or span.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Agent Host was already spawned/restarted with composed OTel environment values; the managed file field was not selected.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host availability waits for the existing spawn; path composition adds only bounded synchronous work.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The fixed-size set of OTel policy fields and one configured file path; work does not scale with workspace size, chat history, or span count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Environment composition is synchronous per spawn. The local host lifecycle remains the existing shared-host/restart path; the diff adds a policy value to that path but no new process fan-out or concurrent setup loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Policy/configuration values are reused through the existing configuration service until a settled update; the child environment and resolved path are recomputed on the next host spawn. There is no new startup cache whose misses fan out.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed code is fixed-size synchronous environment/path composition and the expensive fetch/spawn boundaries already existed.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual policy refresh frequency and host spawn duration vary, but the diff adds no multiplicative startup work or extra boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup regression; the managed field adds bounded work and reuses existing policy delivery and host lifecycle boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Export Agent Host telemetry to an enterprise-managed file during chat sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session, turn-timing, first-response, user-interaction, and decoded OTLP events call `FileForwarder.forwardSpans`, which serializes JSON immediately and queues filesystem work. Chat progress does not await the queue, but `flush` and export durability wait for the serialized queue to drain.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Recursively create the managed output file's parent directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One mkdir call per non-empty telemetry batch, even after the first successful creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: FileForwarder performed no mkdir; each batch proceeded directly to appendFile.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the interactive chat critical path, but serialized ahead of each append and therefore directly increases export throughput cost and flush/shutdown latency.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Append a JSON-lines batch to the configured file.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One append per non-empty host telemetry batch after grouping, serialized by the queue.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing file exporter already appended one JSON-lines payload per batch when file export was configured; the PR makes this route available to managed policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off chat progress but on export durability and flush.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Insert Agent Host-produced or loopback-received spans into SQLite when DB export is separately enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing insert per recorded span; managed native traces are not newly mirrored into SQLite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: DB-enabled Agent Host records were already inserted into SQLite.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing local recording work; managed file routing does not add DB inserts for provider-native traces.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Native Copilot SDK writes provider telemetry to the selected managed file destination.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: SDK-defined batching; one configured destination per provider rather than per policy field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Managed telemetry.filePath did not select the existing SDK file exporter; personal/inherited file configuration could already do so.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Telemetry export is asynchronous to chat in the host integration; exact SDK write scheduling is outside this repository.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective cardinality is one queued append per non-empty decoded or synthetic telemetry batch, after spans in that batch are grouped; long or active sessions produce repeated batches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: `FileForwarder` uses one `Queue`, so mkdir and append operations have effective concurrency 1. This prevents a burst but makes every added operation part of the export/flush critical path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The resolved managed path is fixed for the service lifetime. The new parent-directory setup has no positive cache: cold creation and every warm batch both call recursive mkdir. Failures are retried on later batches, which is useful, but successful setup is also unnecessarily retried.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high for the host forwarder: every non-empty batch reaches an unconditional managed-path mkdir inside a single serialized queue. Native SDK details are not needed for the finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Batch volume and mkdir latency depend on session activity and destination filesystem; network-mounted or slow managed paths make the redundant warm operation more costly. The exact native SDK writer batching is outside the repository.
Scenarios.Verdict: One low-severity repeated-filesystem-work regression was reported: cache successful parent creation while retaining retry after failure.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use a managed collector, switch to managed file export, or explicitly disable managed OTel
Scenarios.CriticalPath: At host spawn, `buildAgentHostOTelEnv` selects exactly one policy route and clears conflicting collector endpoint/protocol/header variables. During export, collector traffic remains on the existing SDK or host-forwarder asynchronous path; managed file selection removes collector calls rather than adding fan-out.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send OTLP batches to a configured collector when the collector route remains active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per existing telemetry batch, serialized in the host forwarder; no per-span network fan-out is added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Collector export already sent batched telemetry. The new managed-file branch suppresses those calls instead of duplicating them.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous telemetry delivery; managed file policy clears this route, and explicit disable removes it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One effective destination per spawned host and telemetry batches already grouped by the SDK/receiver.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Host OTLP forwarding remains serialized by its existing queue; managed file selection does not run collector and file forwarding concurrently. Explicit false clears all destinations and DB activation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Destination choice is fixed in the spawned process environment until the next settled policy-driven replacement. There is no fallback retry cache introduced between file and collector routes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added environment clearing explicitly removes collector endpoints/protocols/headers for managed file and disabled branches.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External collector latency and SDK batching vary, but the changed route selection is mutually exclusive and does not increase request cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable network or concurrency regression; route selection reduces rather than fans out collector boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render Agent Host managed-policy readiness diagnostics
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user-triggered diagnostics action iterates registered policy configurations, inspects policy values, and now reads the small OTel policy tuple to decide whether the protocol gap applies. No subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network work is reached.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of registered policies, with one additional fixed-size OTel composition read when CopilotOtelProtocol is present.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous single-pass map iteration; no queue or parallel work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Reads current configuration service values directly; no cache or retained collection is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path is local registry/configuration inspection only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Policy catalog size can change, but the diff adds one bounded configuration read for one policy case.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; this is a low-frequency diagnostic with constant additional work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 22 changed files and all diff pages. Traced managed-policy startup, destination routing, file export, DB/collector boundaries, and diagnostics. Submitted one introduced repeated-work finding for recursive mkdir on every managed file batch; no concrete regression fix in the PR required blame recording.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
